last_action: JUNIPER IS A WEB APP NOW. The user, the day after installing the first grid build: "I think this ideas are better as web apps. For some reason it make more sense like that, I know the notification an all that, but still." Recorded as DECISIONS.md D13, which SUPERSEDES D1 ("native only, there is no web app") and DEMOTES D7 ("the watering reminder is the product"). The justification is in the project's own record: the reminder, the one feature that required being native, has never fired on real hardware once in the app's life, while the app sat unopened for two months and its build expired. New juniper-web/: Vite + React + plain CSS, no React Native anywhere. 581 lines of pure logic ported BYTE FOR BYTE with 74 of their tests (dryness, watering, stats, cover, today-utils, seed) — keeping those modules RN-free is the only reason this was a day and not a rewrite. juniper-app/ is frozen, not deleted (see its FROZEN.md). THE GRID WAS BUILT AND THEN ACTUALLY LOOKED AT, which changed it three times. (1) The dryness colour was a thin FRAME around a pale pressing, and a frame is too little colour to read across a room; a plant with no photograph now has no mat at all and the silhouette sits straight on the dryness field. The per-plant pressing tone was also a SECOND colour system fighting the first — a clay-toned plant looked warm and thirsty however recently it was watered — so in the grid the tone steps aside. (2) Watering a square sent it FLYING to the far end of the grid, because sorting by thirst re-sorts on every change; you tap a drop and the thing you touched teleports. The order is now frozen while the page is open and recomputed only when the set of plants changes. (3) THE RAMP WAS SILENTLY BROKEN IN CSS, TWICE — see D14. `color-mix()` driven by a custom property, and then a gradient slid by `background-position`, each resolving once at first paint and never again, firing no transition events. Watering updated the store, the DOM, the inline style and the accessibility label and left the square exactly the colour it already was. EVERY TEST PASSED THROUGH BOTH, because no test could see a colour — the same blind spot the native app had with Reanimated mocked. The ramp is now a pure OKLab function in src/lib/ramp.ts with 8 tests that assert the colour directly, including that it saturates past due (D12). Verified: tsc clean, 98 tests across 7 suites, production build 68 kB gzipped (the native bundle was 4.43 MB), and the grid, the watering pour, the expanding card and the whole ramp checked by eye in a browser.
next_action: (1) DEPLOY IT. The web app runs on localhost and nowhere else, which is the single biggest thing standing between this and being used — the entire argument for the pivot was that a URL has no install step, and there is no URL yet. `npm run build` in juniper-web produces a static dist/; Vercel already hosts juniper-website, so it is a project and a domain away. (2) USE IT ON A PHONE, with real plants and real photographs. The ramp's midtones, the pour, the size of the drop target and whether a drifting square reads from across a room have been judged on a laptop, in one browser, by eye. (3) EXPORT, THE MOMENT THERE ARE REAL PLANTS IN IT — the garden lives in one browser on one machine and 'clear site data' destroys it; the export is the only backup that exists. (4) Decide on a PWA manifest + service worker, which is what would let it sit on the home screen and is also the precondition for ever having notifications again. (5) Decide what happens to juniper-app/ — frozen is a decision, deleting it is another, and leaving it ambiguous is the only bad option. (6) GitHub Actions billing is still unverified since 2026-08-30, and the CI workflow now points at a frozen app.

blockers.description: The web app has never been deployed. It exists only on localhost, so the whole premise of the pivot — that a link needs no install step — is so far untested. This gates everything else.

The grid is unvalidated by real use. Whether a square drifting toward dried reads at a glance, whether the pour is satisfying enough to want daily, and whether the midtones sit right are questions only a real garden on a real phone can answer.

Juniper now has no reminders at all. That is a deliberate bet (D13) — the grid is meant to be the reminder — but it is a bet, and the only thing that settles it is whether real use happens without one.

The garden has exactly one copy, in one browser, on one machine. There is no backend and no sync, so clearing site data destroys it. The export button is the entire safety net and has never been used on real data.

CI and the Maestro suite both now point at the frozen native app. The Maestro flows were rewritten on 2026-11-07 and have still never executed a single assertion; they are now testing something that is no longer the product. GitHub Actions billing unverified since 2026-08-30.
